title: Tomato seedling stem and leaf segmentation method based on an improved ResNet architecture
summary: The proposed X-ResNet segmented tomato seedling stems and leaves from 3D point clouds and supported phenotypic measurement. The study reports 95.11% training accuracy, 3.26 percentage points above ResNet18, and manual-measurement correlations of R² 0.941 for plant height, 0.752 for stem diameter, 0.945 for leaf area and 0.943 for leaf inclination; reported absolute percentage errors were below 6%. The abstract does not provide a held-out segmentation accuracy.
ai_technology: X-ResNet point-cloud segmentation with bottleneck, downsampling and specialized convolutional layers
organization: College of Information Technology, Jilin Agricultural University, Changchun, China; College of Information Engineering, Changchun University of Finance and Economics, Changchun, China

evidence.tested: X-ResNet point-cloud segmentation and extracted plant traits were compared with manual measurements. The paper reports trait-specific R² values and errors, 95.11% training accuracy, and an inference time of 4.02 seconds versus 5.37 seconds for ResNet18.
evidence.unknown: The 95.11% value is training accuracy; the abstract does not state held-out segmentation accuracy. Transfer to other cultivars or growing conditions is not established.
evidence.ai_role: The learned X-ResNet segmented tomato stems and leaves from point clouds; the resulting height, diameter, area and inclination estimates were compared with manual measurements.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
